scope: MAGNITUDE RULED OUT: 4096 (a single set bit, larger than 2048) also costs 55 bits, so the 42-bit jump is triggered by a BIT PATTERN
conclusion: five single-bit values spanning bits 8..12 ALL cost 55 bits, including one LARGER than the last flat point
so the cost does not depend on magnitude and not on bit length
5830 is the only expensive value and it is the only one with MULTIPLE low bits set (bits 1, 2) as well as high ones
that points at a per-set-bit or low-bit-pattern cost inside the codec rather than a magnitude threshold
next_candidates: test 6 (bits 1 and 2 only) - if it costs 55, low bits alone are harmless
test 1742 (5830 with bit 12 cleared) - if it costs 97, bit 12 is irrelevant and the low bits carry the cost
test 5830 with the low bits cleared (5830 & ~6 = 5824) - the complement
why_this_is_progress: a magnitude threshold would have required an unbounded search
a bit-pattern trigger is a FINITE question: 32 bits, each testable, and the low-bit pair is the obvious first candidate
